newsitem.title: USA: Washington legislature approves new football stadium.
newsitem.headline: Washington legislature approves new football stadium.

text.p: Gov. Gary Locke signed a bill late Saturday setting up a statewide vote on a financing package to build a new $425 million outdoor stadium for the Seattle Seahawks football team.
Earlier Saturday, the measure passed the Washington State Senate on a vote of 28-21. It passed the state House Friday.

"Let the people of the state of Washington decide whether they want to keep the Seahawks in Seattle," state Sen. Alex Deccio told his colleagues. "If they approve it, the stadium will be built. If they don't, then the Seahawks will leave."
The financing package will be put to voters at a special election June 17.

Voters will be asked to approve new lottery scratch ticket games, to extend the existing hotel-motel tax in King County through the year 2020, to divert some sales tax revenue to the stadium, and to tax tickets and parking there.
Those taxes raise $329 million over 20 years. Prospective Seahawks buyer Paul Allen will chip in another $100 million to complete the package.

Some state representatives sought to add a tax on the highly paid athletes who will play in the new stadium, but that populist idea was shot down because no one else in Washington pays state income tax.

Billionaire Allen made a new stadium a condition of his offer to purchase the Seahawks and secure their future in Seattle. The Microsoft Corp. co-founder spent hundreds of thousands of dollars lobbying the legislature and on television advertising to build public support.

Allen's exhausted lobbyists were in the mood to celebrate. "We're very pleased," said Bert Kolde, vice chairman of Allen's Football Northwest subsidiary. "It looks like we'll have the chance to take this to the people, a chance to make the case why this is a good long-term solution, a fair long-term solution."
Allen's group now have about seven weeks to sell the stadium financing package to voters. Campaign managers are already at work crafting messages to sway skeptical citizens.
